cohort: 2233 pregnant women (754 adolescents aged <20 years and 1479 adults) who delivered singleton newborns at a tertiary health center between January 2018 and June 2022.
finding: Adolescent pregnancies were significantly more complicated with adverse maternal (oligohydramnios, preterm delivery, intravenous iron treatment, perineal injury) and perinatal (fetal growth restriction, lower birth weight, lower first-minute Apgar score, small for gestational age, need for intensive care, neonatal death) outcomes compared to adult pregnancies.
